paradigms.name: Empiricism
paradigms.description: Values observation, perception by sense, and verifiable experiences. Relies on instrumentation, reliability, validation.

paradigms.name: Positivism
paradigms.description: Mechanistic, reductionist principles (complex things are reduced to basic components).
core_beliefs: The goal of science is to explain, predict, and control
Facts can be measured and observed

paradigms.name: Post-positivism
paradigms.description: Focus on rigor and objective inquiry through quantitative methods but recognizes contextual variables

paradigms.name: Phenomenology
description: Seeks to understand the meaning of human experience
Knowledge is grounded in human experience; core similarities form the 'essence'

paradigms.name: Constructivism
description: Knowledge is subjective and created by individuals
Emphasis on subjectivity, multiple truths, trends, patterns, discovery, and understanding

paradigms.name: Postmodernism
description: Rejects a single truth (multiple meanings and ways of knowing)
Knowledge is uncertain, contextual, and relative; changes over time
